findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: REPEAT- The PIC is the only employee present and is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). The PIC has their food handler certificate, but was educated that there always needs to be at least one CFPM in the facility during all hours of food preparation and serving. Ensure that there are enough Certified Food Protection Managers to cover all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: There was a mop bucket of used mop water next to the mop sink. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC who was educated that the waste water needs to be dumped in the mop sink immediately after use, as this prevents pest harborage conditions. Ensure that waste water is dumped immediately after use.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking at the handwashing sink to the right of the ovens is observed to be in disrepair. Discussed re-caulking this by next routine inspection. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: REPEAT- There was a container of food for an employee in the top of the cooler containing hot dogs to the left of the ovens. CORRECTED- The PIC removed the food from the cooler and was educated that the food needs to be in a bottom shelf in a bin labeled personal. Ensure that food intended for employees is kept separate from food for consumers to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager on duty at the facility today. Ensure that there is always at least one CFPM on duty during all hours of operation. 

 (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The soda nozzles were observed to have an accumulation of residue on them. Ensure that all soda nozzles are frequently cleaned. Food contact surfaces should be cleaned to sight and touch. A follow up will be conducted on 8/21/24 to ensure that the soda nozzles have been cleaned. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer water (Quat) was observed to only be at a concentration of 100 ppm. The recommended concentration for Quaternary Ammonium is 200 to 400ppm. Ensure that sanitizer buckets and water are routinely tested and changed if the concentration is low. CORRECTED- The sanitizer water was remade and tested to be at a concentration of 400ppm. 

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FIRST REPEAT- Water bottles are observed to be stored outside of the facility. Storing water bottles outside does not protect them from contamination. Ensure cases of water bottles are stored inside the facility in a clean, dry location. 

FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: The following freezers are observed to have a large accumulation of ice build up:

1. The Breakfast Freezer.
2. The Lunch Freezer. 

Ensure that the ice build up in these freezers is scraped off and the issue is repaired to allow the freezers to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The following areas were observed to be in need of a cleaning: 

1. The fans in the walk-in cooler. 
2. The counter behind the tea station. 
3. The floors underneath the soda syrups. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are cleaned and then maintained cleaned as often as necessary. Physical facilities should be cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean. 

 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: There were chips and salsa that had been opened and eaten by an employee stored on top of food intended for the facility. Ensure that employee storage is located to avoid contamination to food intended for the facility. CORRECTED- The items were moved out of the fridge and into an area away from food intended for the facility. 

(A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Water bottles cases were observed stored outside near the wall of the establishment. This is not considered a clean, dry location for the water bottles. Ensure the water bottles are moved to a clean, dry location where they are protected from possible contamination.
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The mop was stored inside the mop bucket with dirty mop water in the bucket. Ensure the mop is stored in a position that allows it to air dry properly and old mop water is discarded. The mop was moved and water was discarded during the inspection. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: 5-205.11: Observed hand washing sink next to office to be blocked by boxes.  Boxes were moved. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: 4-202.16: Observed ice cream freezer to have a thick layer of frost on interior of freezer.  Defrost ice cream freezer. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed no date marking on whipped topping bag. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) The date marking on the creamer is PLUS seven days instead of Seven Days/Plus 6.  10/11 to 10/28. Also, there is no time indicated on the pre-cooked, wrapped sandwiches for grab and go. Time should have been indicated to pull product at 4 hours (3pm). Label foods properly. Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Wet wiping cloth is observed on coffee service counter. The facility uses cloths with spray bottles, so they should be a single-use towel and go directly into soiled linen after use. Removed during the inspection. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The shelving in the walk-in cooler is coated with mold. Clean the slotted shelving holding sodas/milk. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-151(a) Observed Gehl's cheese and chili sauces to be dated from 5/7.  Food is beyond the allowed seven days. FURTHERMORE:    THE DATE MARKING INDICATED A DISCARD DATE OF 5/14. This is an incorrect application of the Seven Day Rule. 5/7 is Day 1, so seven days becomes 5/13. Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
750-250  Observed a dispenser holding 1/2 and 1/2 and french vanilla creamer to be holding temperature at 70F. Operator found a significant amount of frost accumulation on the lower fans of the unit. This is, no doubt, blocking air flow through the unit. The food was discarded and machine was unplugged to allow for defrost. Food should not be returned to the unit until the machine holds at 41F. All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Facility is using orange cloths with spray bottles. There is the ability to use buckets. Cease using a wiping cloth with a spray bottle. If using cloths, place cloth in sani-bucket of solution between uses. A wet cloth on top of a spray bottle simply grows bacteria between uses. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) A few of the soda nozzles are observed with a slight accumulation of mold on the spout. Clean and sanitize the spouts to remove gross food debris and molds.  To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed several of the shelves in the walk-in cooler (under milk and perishables) to be soiled with molds and food splash. Also, observed the inside of the cappuccino machine to be soiled with accumulated powders.  Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: 750-1120(b) The handsinkin the lobby is observed obstructed by a bucket, cloths, and signage. Employee was in the process of cleaning and left the items to go wait on customers. The handsink remained obstructed from before the arrival of inspector to just before inspector left. Customers were observed moving the bucket to reach handsink. All items removed from sink during the inspection.  Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed multiple roller grill items in the walk in cooler without proper date marking. Date marking requirements were discussed at length with management and detailed in HACCP. A few packages of roller grill items were discarded since the exact date of the package being opened was unknown. A few packages of hot dogs and brats were opened without date marking but according to management all packages were opened within the last 3 days. Items were date marked to correct the violation. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed a pair of soiled tongs at the roller grill station. Facility stated they switch in-use utensils at least once a day. Utensil was switched with a clean one to correct the violation. Switch in-use dispensing utensils at least once every four hours. See details on policy requirement in General Comments.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 1) Observed the basin of the mop sink to be soiled with an accumulation of possible mold. 2) Observed the end of the drain lines from the soda fountains to be soiled with an accumulation of possible mold. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed multiple boxes of single service items stored on the floor of the storage room. Store all single service items at least 6" above the floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
findings.comment:
Observed multiple drain lines from the soda fountains to be draining in to the basin of the mop sink. A physical air gap was provided for drain lines to prevent the possibility of back flow into the equipment.
750-1100 Commercial dishwashing machines, dishwashing sinks, pot washing sinks, pre-rinse sinks, silverware sinks, bar sinks, soda fountain sinks, vegetable sinks, potato peelers, ice machines, steam tables, steam cookers, and other similar fixtures shall be connected in a manner that does not allow for backsiphonage or backflow into the equipment.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed a soiled, wet mop laying on the floor next to the mop sink. Hang mops once soiled to ensure quick drying.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
750-1160 The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed multiple drink items stored on the floor of the walk in cooler. Store all food and drinks at least 6" above the floor.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the basin of the mop sink to be soiled with an accumulation of molds. Clean and maintain this surface.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
findings.comment:
Observed multiple drain lines from the soda fountain and other drink vending machines to be ran along the wall and draining into the basin of the mop sink. Discussed with management about providing a physical air gap to prevent back flow. Drain lines were moved out of the mop sink basin and air gap provided.
750-1080 The potable water system shall be installed to preclude the possibility of backflow.  Devices to protect against backflow and back siphonage shall be installed at all fixtures and equipment where an air gap at least twice the diameter of the water inlet is not provided between the water outlet from the fixture and the fixture’s flood-level rim and wherever else backflow or backsiphonage may occur. Install backflow prevention device.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) Observed the floor under the soda syrup boxes to be soiled with an accumulation of debris. 2) Observed the floor of the walk in cooler to be soiled with an accumulation of packaging debris and some drink splash. Clean and maintain these floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor under shelving in the walk in cooler to be soiled with packaging debris, drink splash, and litter. Clean this floor.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
CORRETED> Observed a coat stored on top of boxes holding service items in the back storage room. Coat was moved to a proper location to correct the violation.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed a wet mop stored in a mop bucket between uses. Hang mops between uses or after use to ensure quick drying.
750-1160 The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents.
